jobs.title: Data Analyst, New Grad
jobs.description:
Jobright is your personal AI job search agent that transforms the way you do job search from solo, time-consuming efforts to a fast, expert-guided journey, simplifying every job search step and accelerating your route to the best job outcomes. As a Data Analyst, New Grad, you will work onsite with product, engineering, and AI teams to turn product, job market, and user data into insights that directly influence product development.

Why Join Us

• Build real, production AI agents used by real users
• High ownership and impact
• Work at the intersection of AI, agents, and product
• Shape how people experience AI-driven job search

Responsibilities

• Analyze product, user, and job market data to identify trends and opportunities
• Write SQL queries and build reports, dashboards, and analytical tools
• Define and monitor key product and business metrics
• Support A/B tests and evaluate new product features
• Investigate data quality issues and improve reporting accuracy
• Present findings to product, engineering, and business stakeholders
• Collaborate closely with the team in an onsite environment
Qualification

Required

• Recent graduate or graduating soon in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Mathematics, Economics, or a related field
• Strong SQL skills and familiarity with spreadsheets or Python
• Understanding of basic statistics, data analysis, and experimentation
• Strong attention to detail and problem-solving skills
• Ability to work onsite in the SF Bay Area

Preferred

• Experience with pandas, scikit-learn, Tableau, Looker, or similar tools
• Familiarity with product analytics, recommendation systems, or search
• Experience working with large or messy datasets
• Previous internship, research, or analytics project experience

jobs.title: Peer Counselor Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
*Job Summary and Responsibilities*

As our *Peer Counselor Program Coordinator*, you will plan, coordinate, implement, and evaluate breastfeeding peer counselor programs for the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), designed to promote maternal and infant nutrition literacy, breastfeeding education and support, and individual and community wellness, working directly with pregnant and breastfeeding mothers in the WIC community.

Every day you will collaborate with community partners and external organizations to coordinate breastfeeding promotion events and programs, oversee the work of WIC Breastfeeding Peer Counselors, and serve as a liaison between WIC participants, healthcare providers, and other support agencies, developing strategies and resources in conjunction with community agencies, high schools, and groups in accordance with grant provisions.

To be successful in your role, you will need strong organizational, communication, and computer skills, including database management, along with independent and critical thinking, creativity, and discretion to navigate varied and evolving work situations.

Plans, coordinates, implements and evaluates the grant-funded breastfeeding peer counselor program in accordance with grant provisions and requirements.
Participates in identification of community health promotion needs and development/implementation of promotion activities related to WIC breastfeeding education and support.
Designs/develops health activities/tools for WIC communities/groups to effectively meet breastfeeding promotion needs.
Recruits community organizations for partnering on breastfeeding and maternal and infant nutrition education initiatives.
Collaborates on program marketing efforts including flier development, PowerPoint presentations, social marketing, etc.
Participates in development of grant applications and assists with data input, analysis and quarterly/annual reporting; attends training, meetings and other events hosted by granting agencies.
Job Requirements*Required
Bachelors Other in Health Education/Promotion or related field and two (2) years’ experience in community outreach, program planning and evaluation, upon hire and
one years’ experience providing breastfeeding support or
Five (5) years’ experience in health education and/or public health or community outreach, with experience in nutrition, physical activity, food justice, prevention programming, planning and evaluation or related experience and
one year experience in providing breastfeeding support and
International Board Certified Lactation Consultant, upon hire

Where You'll Work

Virginia Mason Franciscan Health has a rich history of providing exceptional healthcare, dating back to 1891. Building upon a legacy of compassionate care and innovation, our organization has evolved over the years through strategic partnerships and integrations to expand our reach and services across the Puget Sound area.

Today, as Virginia Mason Franciscan Health, we remain deeply committed to healing the whole person – body, mind, and spirit – in the communities we serve. This commitment is strengthened by the diverse expertise and shared values brought together through our growth.

Our dedicated providers offer a full spectrum of health care services, from routine wellness to complex disease management, all grounded in rigorous research and education. Our comprehensive network of 10 hospitals and nearly 300 care sites strategically located across the greater Puget Sound region reflects our ongoing commitment to accessibility and comprehensive care.

We are proud of our pioneering medical advances and numerous awards and accreditations that reflect our dedication to excellence. When you join Virginia Mason Franciscan Health, you become part of a team that delivers top-quality, professional healthcare in modern, well-equipped facilities, and contributes to a legacy of service built on collaboration and shared purpose.

*Pay Range*

$29.44 - $48.57 /hour

jobs.title: Field Technician / General Laborer – Custom Home Building
jobs.description:
About The Position

Are you a hardworking, dependable team player who takes pride in building things the right way? Do you want to learn the custom home building trade from the ground up alongside a fourth-generation team that has been doing it since 1947? Are you looking for a place where showing up, working hard, and caring about the details actually matters? Imagine a role where every day you contribute to building some of the finest custom homes in the Lake Minnetonka area.

If this sounds like the opportunity you’ve been looking for, please read on to learn more about this position!

Core Values

Ethical
Motivating
Positive Attitude
Passionate About Details and Consistency
Humble
Servant Leadership
Take Initiative and Drive to Completion

Position overview

We are seeking a reliable Field Technician / General Laborer to support our jobsite teams across all phases of custom home construction. This role keeps our sites running, handling material movement, site cleanliness, basic construction tasks, and hands-on support for carpenters, subcontractors, and the project superintendent. You will be a key part of keeping projects safe, organized, and on schedule, with plenty of opportunity to learn and grow into the trade.

Key Responsibilities

Site Support: Load, unload, move, and stage materials, tools, and equipment as directed.
Jobsite Cleanliness & Safety: Maintain clean, organized, and safe work areas; remove debris and manage waste daily.
General Construction Tasks: Assist with demolition, basic framing support, blocking, backing, and other hands-on tasks under supervision.
Tool & Equipment Care: Operate hand and power tools safely; help maintain and account for tools and equipment.
Crew Assistance: Support carpenters, subcontractors, and the superintendent to keep work moving efficiently.
Site Readiness: Help with material deliveries, basic measurements, and prep work to keep the schedule on track.

Education, Experience, And Skills Required

Reliable transportation and consistent, on-time attendance.
Ability to follow directions and work as part of a team.
Basic familiarity with hand and power tools (preferred, not required—willing to train the right person).
A strong work ethic and willingness to learn the trade.

Compensation

Liberal PTO Policy
Medical insurance with 80% coverage for employee-only plans (family coverage paid by employee)
401k plan with a 3% company match
Mileage Reimbursement

Personal Characteristics needed to perform this role

Dependability: Shows up on time, ready to work, every day.
Work Ethic: Takes pride in hard work and getting the job done right.
Attitude: Positive, coachable, and a good teammate.
Physical Requirements: Ability to perform physical labor in all weather conditions, lift up to 50+ lbs, and navigate construction sites including climbing ladders and scaffolding.
Core Values: Alignment with our core values in all aspects of work.

Not Applicable

Full-time

Engineering and Information Technology

jobs.title: Data Analyst I
jobs.description:
Our mission is to enhance the health of our community and to achieve this we provide health services that address unmet needs and opportunities. We demonstrate dignity and respect for all people and focus on our employees, clients and community.  Join our organization and help us accomplish our goals and make a meaningful impact in our community!

We believe that our people are our greatest strength. Each employee contributes to our shared mission, vision, strategy, and values. We are committed to fostering a workplace that is Supportive
, Impactful
, Accountable
, and Inclusive
.

Are you interested in working in a place where your contributions and ideas are valued? A place where you can serve with compassion, make a difference in people’s lives, and pursue excellence?
Are you proficient with analytic tools and platforms? The Health District is seeking a Data Analyst I
to join our team. The Analyst plays a key role in helping programs, leadership, and community partners improve performance, equity and outcomes through data.  This position coordinates and implements standard-to-moderately complex analytic projects and supports community health assessment.

Compensation & Benefits

$62,720 – $76,832 annually (DOQ)
Comprehensive benefits package
Professional development opportunities

Schedule & Environment

40 hours per week, Monday- Friday (Exempt)
Primarily office-based with occasional meaningful community engagement

For full qualifications and responsibilities, please review the job description at
www.healthdistrict.org/careers.
Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in public health, statistics, data analytics, epidemiology, or related field.
Minimum of 5-7 years of experience, demonstrated ability, and skills in health data, analytics, or reporting.
Equivalent combination of education and experience level

Key Responsibilities

Develop, improve and maintain analytic queries, calculations, reports and visualizations that support program evaluation, service quality, strategic planning, and decision-making.
Distill and translate quantitative and qualitative data into clear, usable insights for non-technical audiences including staff, board members, and the community.
Stay abreast of emerging trends, technologies, and methodologies in data analytics.

How to Apply

If you are interested in applying, we encourage you to think broadly about your background and skill set for the role and include relevant knowledge, skills, abilities, education, work, and lived/ living experience. Please include a cover letter
that details how your experiences and qualifications align with this position.

Submit a resume and cover letter
to Attn: Search Coordinator
Email:
searchcoordinator@healthdistrict.org
Mail:
Health District of Northern Larimer County, 120 Bristlecone Drive, Fort Collins, CO 80524

The anticipated close date is Sunday, August 30, 2026.

Why work for us

We value a work-life balance
Employees are encouraged to develop their skills and knowledge that result in successful performance in their roles/positions
Medical/Dental benefits: employee covered at 100%; dependents covered at 75%
Low-cost vision plan available
Retirement plan 401(a): employee contribution (3%); employer contribution (5%)
An optional 457(b) retirement plan is available
Generous flexible paid time off. Earn 20 days of PTO in the 1 st year and 13 paid holidays; 40 hours of sick leave is provided (employees hired after June 30 of a calendar year will receive 20 hours of sick leave for that year). PTO is prorated per FTE.
Intermediate paid leave benefits to eligible employees in lieu of the State of Colorado FAMLI plan
Employee Assistance Programs (EAPs) that provide confidential and free support to our staff
Access to legal and financial counseling
Up to six counseling sessions per issue for mental health concerns
Variety of additional resources
Federal Student Loan Forgiveness is available for qualifying borrowers
We offer a yearly allowance for professional growth.
We believe that diverse backgrounds and perspectives strengthen our organization, so we consider a combination of experiences to meet minimum qualifications. Experience may include related knowledge, skills, abilities, education, work, and lived/living experience
We are committed to creating an equitable and inclusive workplace and proudly serves as an Equal Opportunity Employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and ensure that all qualified candidates receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ethnic or national origin, ancestry, age, sex, pregnancy, disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion (creed), political beliefs, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws

Infection Prevention

During flu season, flu shots are strongly recommended for this position.
